findings.claim: fomo.family's 'copy trading' is notification-based and manual: following a trader gives you push alerts when they buy/sell, and you decide whether to place the same trade yourself. There is no auto-mirroring, no sizing engine and no execution delay setting inside the fomo app.
findings.evidence: fomo's own answer page: users 'decide whether to execute each trade' and this 'differs from mirror trading which automatically replicates trades without your input'. fomo's 'how to start copy trading' page: 'turn on notifications for traders you follow' and receive 'instant alerts when a trader buys or sells'. Datawallet: 'social trading, not automated copy trading'. fomobyte guide: copy trading 'operates manually'. Bankless: Se Park hopes 'radical transparency' curbs traders who 'accumulate tokens from private wallets, buy publicly on Fomo to broadcast conviction, and exit as soon as followers arrive'. NOTE: docs.onfomo.com/trading/copy (Smart Setup, 0.5x-5x scaling, TP/SL, reverse copy, v2.0.0 'Copy Trade Launch' Mar 24 2026) is a DIFFERENT product (onfomo.com, a Hyperliquid perps app) and search engines conflate it with fomo.family; some third-party reviews (BTCC, fomobyte review) loosely say 'automatically mirror' but no primary fomo.family source describes automation.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Follower flow is human-latency (open push, tap, confirm) so it arrives seconds-to-minutes after the leader's fill, spread out rather than in one block. A bot on the on-chain stream can front-run the manual copier wave; conversely there is no mechanical 'follower auto-buy' to guarantee post-signal demand.

findings.claim: Feed/alert latency: fomo's in-app feed and push alerts lag the on-chain fill by roughly 15 seconds (sometimes >20s); the fomoapi.io on-chain stream (Growth $499/mo) sees the trade ~2s after the block, i.e. ~15s before the app shows it. The app feed itself (fomoapi /ws/alerts, all plans) delivers what users see at the same moment they see it.
findings.evidence: fomoapi blog: 'the typical lead was a little over 15 seconds. Some trades showed up on-chain more than 20 seconds before the app mentioned them'; on-chain stream trades arrive 'about two seconds after the block'; feed generation described as 'FOMO then notices the trade, decides whether it clears the bar for the feed, writes the feed item, and pushes it out to phones'. No sample sizes/percentiles are published. Odaily practical guide: 'FOMO's signals reach you with a delay ... if it's already pumped 10%-20%, this is essentially not the same trade anymore.' fomoscan: 'By the time a trade is visible, posted and copied, the person you are copying may already be selling into the flow your copy created.'
findings.relevance_to_strategy: A ~15s head start over every app user on a 100ms-block chain is the single clearest structural edge available to a retail bot; the payoff depends on whether follower buying actually moves price in the following minutes (see separate finding).

findings.claim: What qualifies as a 'large buy' alert is not published; fomo decides the threshold server-side. Notification categories exposed by fomo: price alerts (e.g. 'TOKEN up 2x since verification', type PRICE_SINCE_LISTED), trade opens/closes, whale/large buys and sells (type LARGE_BUY), profit milestones, follows, 'trending activity' (a coin 'being bought by a lot of traders'), 'top traders' activity (large trades)', and 'friends' activity' filterable by a user-set minimum trade size.
findings.evidence: fomo blog 'Leveraging fomo's social features' lists six notification types incl. friends' activity 'filterable by trade size minimum', trending activity 'when a coin is being bought by a lot of traders', and top traders' activity '(large trades)', with no dollar thresholds. fomoapi openapi/docs: notification_type examples PRICE_SINCE_LISTED and LARGE_BUY; alert payload {alertType: buy|sell|thesis|whale|price|trade, source: feed|push, usdValue, chainId, chain, tokenAddress}. fomoapi alerts blog: a large-buy is 'a position change above a size threshold' with no USD number disclosed; example text 'cupsey opened a 4.2 SOL position in PONS at a 1.1M market cap'. fomoapi whale-bot guides use a user-chosen MIN_USD (example $2,500).
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Because the push threshold is opaque, the strategy should infer it empirically from /v2/notifications (LARGE_BUY events vs usdValue) rather than assume a fixed cutoff; alerts with source='push' reach every follower's phone and are the demand-shock candidates worth modelling.

findings.claim: fomo fee schedule (verified Aug 20 2026): Solana tiered (under 5 USDC flat 0.10; 5-47.50 USDC 2%; 47.50-190 USDC flat 0.95; 190+ USDC 0.50%); Base, BNB Chain, Monad and Robinhood Chain flat 0.50% per trade; Ethereum 0.50% plus network fees passed through; select majors 0.05% (>=1,000 USDC) with <=0.50 USDC minimum below that; 0.45% with a referral code (10% off); perps 0.05% builder fee on top of venue fees. fomo covers 'all gas fees, priority fees, and token rent' on Solana, Base, BNB, Monad and Robinhood Chain. Smallest sellable position $2. ToS: third-party protocol fees and slippage are the user's responsibility; slippage is auto-set (no manual control) per user guides.
findings.evidence: fomoappguide fee page (last verified 2026-08-20) gives the per-chain bands and the gas statement; Datawallet: gas 'sponsored by Fomo', ERC-4337 paymaster pays gas; TechCrunch (Nov 2025): 0.50%, $0.95 minimum on Solana, no minimum on Base/BNB, no gas charged; fomobyte: slippage 'automatically calculated ... users cannot manually set it'; fomo ToS Section 7: fees displayed pre-confirmation, gas/protocol fees/slippage borne by user. Insights4VC: a $10 order faces ~9.5% explicit fee on Solana.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Round trip on Robinhood Chain via fomo = ~1.0% app fee (0.9% with referral) + 2x1% Pons pool fee + price impact; a bot trading directly on Uniswap V3 pays only the 1% pool fee each way plus sub-cent gas, a ~1 pt/round-trip cost advantage over app copiers.

findings.claim: On Robinhood Chain fomo's exact swap router is not publicly documented. What is documented: fomo uses ERC-4337 account abstraction with a paymaster (gas sponsored, batched ops), Relay for cross-chain balance/bridging, DFlow order-flow auctions on Solana for MEV protection, and swaps execute against on-chain DEX liquidity (no internal book). Uniswap v2/v3/v4 + UniswapX are live on Robinhood Chain (Universal Router 2.1.1 at 0x8876789976decbfcbbbe364623c63652db8c0904; SwapRouter02 at 0xcaf681a66d020601342297493863e78c959e5cb2) and fomo was a day-one third-party venue for Uniswap's Pools.trade launchpad. The wallet shown on a fomo profile is a Privy signer with ~zero txs; real trades settle from a separate 'real' EVM wallet, so on-chain attribution requires wallet resolution.
findings.evidence: Datawallet: ERC-4337 paymaster, DFlow, Relay, decentralized liquidity; Relay docs: gasless swaps via 4337/7702; Uniswap deployments page lists router addresses; The Defiant/Yahoo: fomo among day-one venues for Pools.trade; fomoapi docs/blog: 'The address it shows is a custodial Privy wallet with zero transactions', real wallet resolved via /v2/users/{handle}; on-chain stream tags 'verified: db|relay|code'. Aug 30 2026: cross-chain trades/deposits degraded due to 'a bridge partner's liquidity issue' (X trend summary), consistent with Relay dependency.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Any 'follow fomo flow on-chain' detector must key off resolved real wallets (fomoapi/fomoscan) or a fomo fee-recipient/paymaster signature rather than the profile address; identifying fomo's paymaster/fee payer on Blockscout is an open task before backtesting on Helius-equivalent Robinhood data.

findings.claim: Robinhood Chain execution environment: Arbitrum Orbit/Nitro L2, chain id 4663, ~100 ms block time, first-come-first-served sequencer with no priority gas auction ('increasing your fee will not shift your transaction ahead'), ETH gas, EIP-1559, two-part fee (L2 execution + L1 data). A split-routed Uniswap swap on 2026-07-15 used 135,568 gas at ~0.068 gwei = 0.0000092 ETH (<2 US cents); trackers on 2026-09-03 show 0.3-2.3 gwei. Chain-wide fees hit a record $3.75M on Sep 1 (mostly Pons/launchpad fee layers, not base gas). Robinhood Wallet (not fomo) subsidizes swap gas until ~Sep 29 2026.
findings.evidence: docs.robinhood.com: FCFS sequencing, two-component fees, ERC-4337 first-class; KuCoin/Datawallet: 100 ms blocks; splitshot.finance: concrete swap gas example; hood-chain.com gas tracker 0.33-0.49 gwei, robinscan 2.3 gwei; cryptonomist/cryptobriefing: $3.75M daily fees Sep 1, $13M cumulative; KuCoin flash: fees rose from ~$56K/day (Aug 23) to $3.75M (Sep 1) driven by volume and Pons fee stacking; Robinhood gas subsidy threshold cut from $5 to $0.50 for Robinhood Wallet swaps, program ends late September.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Gas is negligible for a bot (cents), so fee drag is entirely the 1% Pons pool fee + impact. FCFS ordering means latency to the sequencer, not gas bidding, decides who fills first; Pons' 2-block launch protection is only ~200 ms of wall-clock at 100 ms blocks.

findings.claim: Pons launchpad mechanics (V1, the dominant format): fixed 1B supply minted into a one-sided locked Uniswap V3 position from block one, 1% pool fee (70% creator / 30% protocol on new launches; 90/10 legacy), 0.0005 ETH launch fee, launch-block only the creator's atomic dev buy executes, and during the first two blocks a wallet cannot hold >5% of supply or buy >5.5% ('same-block block, max wallet, cumulative buy cap'); no restrictions on sells/transfers; 'graduation' at 4.2 WETH paired is cosmetic (pool is already live). V2 adds a bonding curve (<=10% curve fee + <=10% creator tax) graduating into a locked Uniswap v4 pool. Pons took ~59-64% of launchpad activity/fees on the chain in late Aug (17,909 of 27,802 launches on Aug 31; $4.89M fees Aug 31).
findings.evidence: GitHub ponsdotdev/ponsfamily README (factories 0xA5aAb3F0c6EeadF30Ef1D3Eb997108E976351feB V1, 0x7eD598BcEf8bd9Edd8C97A195C6d13f40801EC7e V2, anti-snipe description, fee caps); KuCoin blog (5%/5.5% limits, creator-only launch block, 4.2 ETH graduation, 1B supply, fee split); The Defiant (1% pool fee 70/30, 80% of protocol share to PONS buybacks, Uniswap Pools.trade 0.25% LP fee rival); The Defiant Sep 1 (Pons fee share).
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Concentrated one-sided V3 liquidity with no curve means price impact is set by the launch preset tick range; sells are never restricted, so a leader can dump into follower flow at any time. The 5.5% cumulative cap only binds for 2 blocks, so sniping is not structurally prevented.

findings.claim: Credit-card memecoin flow (The Block, 2026-09-01): Crossmint powers Apple Pay/Google Pay/card checkout in fomo and Robinhood Wallet with no separate KYC; ~150 tokens supported (~80% of 24h memecoin volume); purchases were coded MCC 5815 'digital goods media' rather than crypto MCCs 6012/6051, so they earned card rewards and were not flagged as crypto; Chase called it an incorrect category and opened a Visa case; the NY AG is reviewing. Crossmint is ~7% of fomo user inflows; 68,000+ first-time crypto buyers via Apple Pay; weekly active traders using the checkout rose 7x after the June launch (325 -> 2,400+). Tokens are delivered directly to the user's app wallet. Card fees/limits are undisclosed (Crossmint pricing is quote-only).
findings.evidence: The Block article (MCC 5815, Chase/Visa case, NY AG, Crossmint quote 'only game in town ... no KYC'); Crossmint case study ($4B volume, 625K users, 68K first-time buyers, 7x weekly active traders 325->2,400+, 'token lands in their wallet instantly', 197 countries); eco.com fee comparison: Crossmint card pricing is custom/quote-only, fiat routed via MoonPay/Banxa-type partners with 1-1.5% FX spread (low confidence on the spread applying to fomo).
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Card-funded buyers are price-insensitive, latency-slow retail demand concentrated in ~150 whitelisted tokens; a regulatory/card-network clampdown (Visa case, NY AG) is a live risk that could abruptly remove a chunk of inflow, so the strategy should not depend on it.

findings.claim: Follower scale: fomo reports 1.9M+ users (30K/day added), 1.2M active in August, ~$2.8B monthly volume and ~$17M monthly revenue; Bankless: ~30% of signups become traders. On Robinhood Chain fomo had ~64K daily active addresses, ~$101M/day (~36% of chain volume), 'one in every two active wallets', avg ~$1,565/address/day. Leaderboard follower counts (fomoapi snapshot in this repo, 2026-09): top-100 median ~10-15K followers; top 10 have 178K-498K; #1 unipcs ~466K followers (peer.family shows 460K) with $12.3M all-time PnL on $2.36M volume and 2,542 trades.
findings.evidence: Dealroom (Mobula acquisition): 1.9M users, 1.2M active Aug, $500M Jun -> $1.5B Jul -> $2.8B Aug pace, ~$17M/mo revenue; ChainCatcher: 64K DAA, $101M/day, 36% share, $1,565/address; Bankless: 650K signups, ~30% traders; local files data/raw/fomoapi/leaderboards/{24h,7d,30d,all}.json (followers field); peer.family/t/unipcs: 460K followers, $11.8M PnL; unipcs on X claims #1 24h/7d and 'first person ever to hit $10m+ in PNL exclusively through spot trades' per fomo team.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: With top leaders at 200-500K followers and tokens at $1-10M caps in 1%-fee V3 pools, even a 0.1% follower conversion at $100 each is $20-50K of taker flow, comparable to pool depth; the on-chain stream lets a bot position before that wave.

findings.claim: Direct quantitative evidence that follower buying moves price on fomo is NOT published; the evidence is qualitative and consistent. fomo co-founder Se Park concedes leaders can 'buy publicly on Fomo to broadcast conviction, and exit as soon as followers arrive'; fomoscan warns the leader 'may already be selling into the flow your copy created'; Odaily advises skipping if a signal is already +10-20% by the time it arrives; CASHCAT rose ~1,300-1,900% on 2026-07-08 after Vlad Tenev's post with 'thin liquidity pools relative to hype' where 'a single large trade could influence pricing noticeably'. FomoTop (independent tracker, 111 wallets, 2,253 picks) finds 53% of tracked traders' first buys peak >= +50% within 48h, but it is selection-based (not realized PnL) and does not isolate follower impact.
findings.evidence: Bankless interview quote; fomoscan copy-trading page; Odaily guide; KuCoin CASHCAT article and coingape; FomoTop methodology page (win = coin peaked >= +50% in 48h; 'Copy ROI is a simulation, not a promise').
findings.relevance_to_strategy: The 'front-run the follower wave' thesis needs to be measured ourselves (event study: price path 0-15s vs 15s-10min after a top-follower leader's on-chain buy, split by follower count and pool depth); nothing public quantifies it, and the co-founder explicitly describes the leader-dumps-on-followers pattern.

findings.claim: PnL/leaderboard computation is not formally documented by fomo. Public statements: leaderboards rank by 'Total P&L ... net profit over a given period' across 24h/7D/30D/all-time and 'all trading data is verified on-chain'; ToS calls them 'Metrics' and reserves the right to recalculate and change methodology. Third-party critique (@MidCurveMortal, relayed by KuCoin, late Aug 2026): fomo 'advertis[es] ALL holdings as profit on INFINITE liquidity' and the #1 trader unipcs' price-impact-adjusted PnL is only ~25% of the displayed figure. fomoapi passes PnL 'exactly as fomo.family reports it' (labels leaderboard pnlUsd 'realized' but per-trade objects carry both realizedPnlUsd and unrealizedPnlUsd).
findings.evidence: fomo answers page on leaderboards; fomo ToS Section 9; KuCoin insight summarising MidCurveMortal post 2094205331895181333; fomoapi docs/llms-full.txt ('PnL is reported by fomo.family, not recomputed here'; trade fields realizedPnlUsd / unrealizedPnlUsd); FomoTop explicitly refuses to use fomo PnL ('these are not realised or unrealised gains').
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Confirms the earlier finding that leaderboard PnL is mark-to-market on illiquid bags; trader selection must be re-scored on realized/exit-adjusted PnL from resolved wallets, and the 75% haircut on the #1 trader is a useful prior for how inflated top ranks are.

findings.claim: No publicly documented case of fomo disqualifying a leaderboard entry was found. What exists: (a) ToS Section 9 bans 'selective transfers of tokens between wallets, wash trading, coordinated activity with other accounts, or exploiting any technical feature' and allows fomo to 'disqualify, adjust, reverse, or void' Metrics and claw back rewards; (b) the Privy-signer/real-wallet split makes selective transfers into the fomo-tracked wallet technically easy (fomoscan: 'A trader can run several wallets and show you only the good one'; 'Concentrated, sudden follower growth is worth a second look'); (c) fomoapi documents a 'retract' message when a pending wallet 'proves to be another app's'; (d) fomo removed X links from profiles; (e) growth was giveaway/leaderboard-competition driven with acknowledged spam-account risk; (f) Aug 24 2026 'malicious iOS update / $6M losses' allegation was denied by co-founder Prashan Dharmasena as 'paid fud'; (g) Aug 30 2026 bridge-partner liquidity outage; (h) Trustpilot/App Store reviews allege the app freezes during LP pulls and that 'many scam tokens [are] verified with a blue tick' (fomo says verification 'is informational only, not an endorsement').
findings.evidence: fomo ToS; fomoscan copy-trading page; fomoapi docs (retract); fomoapi blog on removed Twitter links; asksurf.ai growth analysis; cryptonews.net iOS incident (Aug 24 2026); X trend summary of Aug 30 outage; uk.trustpilot.com fomo.family reviews (2.5/5, Jul 22 and Aug 16 2026 quotes); fomo X post on token verification.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Leader track records can be curated (private accumulation, wallet selection) without triggering visible enforcement, so 'top of leaderboard' is a weak skill signal and a possible adversarial one; operational risk (app freezes, bridge outages ~10 incidents in August per user complaints) argues for executing the bot directly on-chain rather than through the app.

findings.claim: fomoapi.io product facts relevant to the data pipeline: /ws/alerts (all plans; free = realtime for 7 days then 15s delayed) mirrors the app feed with fields alertType (buy/sell/thesis/whale/price/trade), source (feed/push), usdValue, chainId; /ws/trades (Growth $499/mo, 1M req/mo, 2,000 wallet resolutions) is the on-chain stream for Robinhood + Solana only with txHash, block, blockTs, seenAt, latencyMs, token mcap and filters chain/trader/token/minUsd/side; /v2/users/{handle} returns live followers, following, accountAgeDays, averageHoldTimeSeconds, pnl by window, real Solana+EVM wallets; /v2/users/{handle}/trades gives realizedPnlUsd and (for 'captured' trades) avgEntry/avgExit/unrealizedPnlUsd; /v2/notifications exposes fomo's mobile pushes incl. LARGE_BUY. Competing resellers: fomoscope ($0-35/mo, 15s refresh, REST only) and fomoscan (identity/follow graph).
findings.evidence: fomoapi.io landing, /docs, and the repo copy docs/llms-full.txt + docs/openapi.json; fomoscope.xyz pricing page; fomoscan.sh.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: averageHoldTimeSeconds, accountAgeDays and follower counts are available per trader for the skill-vs-luck screen; latencyMs on the on-chain stream lets us measure our own reaction budget before the ~15s app wave.

open_questions: Which contract/fee-payer executes fomo swaps on Robinhood Chain (Universal Router vs SwapRouter02 vs a fomo relay, and the ERC-4337 paymaster address)? Needed to tag fomo flow on Blockscout; fomoapi's 'verified: relay|code' hints at Relay-based fills but nothing public confirms it.

What USD (or % of position / % of pool) threshold does fomo use for LARGE_BUY / 'whale' push notifications, and does it scale with token market cap? Infer empirically from /v2/notifications vs usdValue.

Quantify follower price impact: event-study of price and net taker flow in the 0-15s, 15s-2min and 2-10min windows after buys by leaders bucketed by follower count and pool depth, using resolved real wallets on chain 4663.

How does fomo mark PnL for the leaderboard (last trade price vs pool spot, whether transfers-in are treated as zero-cost basis, whether closed and open positions are combined), and how large is the 'exit-adjusted' haircut across the top 100, not just unipcs?
Is Robinhood Chain's sequencer FCFS purely by arrival time with no Timeboost express lane enabled? If Timeboost is on, a bot could buy priority; docs say FCFS but do not mention Timeboost.
Does the ~15s app lag vary by chain, by trade size, or by whether the token is 'verified' (fomo 'decides whether it clears the bar for the feed')? Only anecdotal measurement exists.
What happens to Robinhood Chain gas and fomo's paymaster subsidy after Robinhood's wallet gas subsidy ends ~Sep 29 2026 — could fomo start passing gas through or raise fees?
What share of fomo's Robinhood Chain volume is card-funded (Crossmint ~7% of inflows overall) and how exposed is that inflow to the Visa/Chase/NY AG review of the MCC 5815 classification?

findings.claim: IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the established facts: Pons has two generations. Pons V1 (deployed Jul 13, 2026) is the 'no bonding curve, fixed 1B supply, Uniswap V3 pool at 1% fee, 2-block launch protection' design. Pons V2 (first launches Aug 3-4, 2026) replaced that with an ETH-denominated constant-product bonding curve (phantom/virtual quote reserve sets opening price) that graduates at a 4.2 ETH threshold into a permanently locked full-range Uniswap v4 pool (pool fee tier 0; a Pons hook charges the fee instead). By Aug 31 the V2 protocol ('Pons') earned $4.89M/day vs 'Pons V1' $508K/day, so the large majority of current launches and fees are V2 curve tokens, not V3-pool tokens.
findings.evidence: docs.ponsfamily.com (V1 page): 'There is no bonding curve and no migration later'; V3 pool, 1% fee, 0.0005 ETH launch fee, 2-block protection, 4.2 ETH graduation. docs.ponsfamily.com/v2: constant-product curve amountOut=(in*reserveOut)/(reserveIn+in), phantom quote reserve, graduation into locked v4 position (locker 0x267444D0...), hook 0xE5e70264..., v4 pool fee tier zero. The Defiant (Aug 6): 'Pons v2 (Aug. 3 launch): Bonding curve graduating to locked Uniswap v4 pool'; The Defiant (Sep 1): launchpad fees Aug 31 -> Pons $4.89M, Pons V1 $508,139. Bitquery docs list Pons factory 0x7ed598bc... as 'bonding curve with graduation to Uniswap v4'.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Any backtest or execution model must branch on V1 vs V2 token: V2 tokens have a curve phase (deterministic price path, same graduation pool size/price for all launches on the same settings) then a v4 hook pool; V1 tokens trade in a V3 1%-fee pool from block 0. Contract addresses: V1 factory 0x0c37a24F... (legacy) / 0xA5aAb3F0...; V2 factory 0x7eD598Bc...; events CurveBuy/CurveSell/CurveCompleted/PoolGraduated on V2.

findings.claim: Pons V2 anti-snipe design: an opening 'snipe tax' starts at 99% of a buy and decays exponentially to zero over the first 5 seconds after launch (about 50 blocks at 100 ms), capped so the buyer nets at least 1% of spend; the launcher/creator-fee recipient plus up to 32 addresses fixed at creation are exempt. V1 instead had a 2-block window (block 0 creator-only; blocks 1-2 max 5% holdings / 5.5% buy per wallet). In V2, trading restrictions apply only to dev wallets; ordinary wallets trade freely.
findings.evidence: docs.ponsfamily.com/v2: snipe tax 'starts at 99% of a buy and decays exponentially to zero across the first 5 seconds'; exemptions for launcher, creator fee recipient and up to 32 addresses. crypto.news V2 announcement: 'Trading restrictions remain configurable only for developer wallets; all other wallets trade freely'; 3-day timelock on CTO. docs.ponsfamily.com V1 page: 2-block window rules.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Block-0/second-0 sniping on V2 is economically punished (99% tax), but the creator plus up to 32 whitelisted wallets can buy tax-free at open, i.e., V2 structurally enables 'bundled' insider allocations. For a retail follower, buying inside the first 5 s is strictly dominated by waiting; the earliest sensible entry is >5 s after launch, and the presence of whitelisted early buyers is a detectable feature (exempt addresses are fixed at creation).

findings.claim: Pons fee economics: 1% trade fee on both the curve and post-graduation pool; split 70% to creator / 30% to protocol for V2 launches (legacy V1 launches incl. PONS itself: 90/10); 80% of the protocol share is TWAP-bought into PONS and burned (not yet immutable); launch fee 0.0005 ETH. Optional creator tax up to ~10% can be added at launch in V2. Creators had been paid ~$20.9M over the first 47 days.
findings.evidence: docs.ponsfamily.com: 70/30 from block 8991118; legacy 90/10 from block 8600612; buyback 80% of protocol fees. KuCoin PONS guide: '80% allocation is not yet immutable'. Bitrue: 'Launchpad curve fees: 1%, Creator taxes: up to 10%, Uniswap v4 hook charges: 1%'. Chaincatcher: token creator payouts ~$20.93M over 47 days.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Round-trip cost on a Pons token via fomo is ~1% Pons fee + ~0.5% fomo fee per side, i.e. ~3% round trip before slippage and any creator tax (up to 10% extra per side on taxed tokens). Strategies must clear >3-5% per trade; creator-tax tokens should be filtered out or priced in (tax is readable on-chain and fixed at launch).

findings.claim: Pons launch volume and graduation rates: daily launches ran ~700-3,300 for most of August, then went vertical in the final week (22,581 on Aug 30; 17,909 of 27,802 chain-wide on Aug 31; ~25,000 on Sep 2). Cumulative Pons launches ~646,000 from ~167,000 unique creator addresses since July (CoinDesk) / 124,016 V2 launches since Aug 3 with 1,362 graduations = 1.10% (Bitquery vs chain data, Aug 31); Aug 25-31: 83,962 launches, 1,064 graduations = 1.27%. Earlier V1 snapshot (Jul 22): ~67,000 launches, 529 graduations (<0.8%), and only 1 graduated token (YOLO) above $5M market cap. Pons captured ~59% of chain launch activity on Sep 1 and ~68% on peak days.
findings.evidence: The Defiant/Bitquery via search: 'Daily launches on Pons sat between 700 and 3,300 for most of August... 22,581 launches on August 30th'; 'Lifetime (from Aug 3) 124,016 tokens, 1.10% graduation'; Aug 25-31 83,962 launches / 1,064 grads. CoinDesk Sep 3 (via snippet): ~646,000 tokens from >167,000 creator addresses. KuCoin/Foresight Jul 22: 67k launched, 529 graduated, only YOLO >$5M. Cryptorank/Dune adam_tehc: 17,909 of 27,802 on Aug 31; 59% share Sep 1. ponslaunchpad.com: 167,354 launched / 2,334 graduated (live counter, date unclear).
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Base rate for a random Pons launch reaching the 4.2 ETH pool is ~1%; reaching >$5M is on the order of 1 in 10,000+. Any launch-sniping/early-entry strategy is a lottery with extreme negative skew; the tradeable universe is the ~1% graduated set (roughly 150-300 per day at late-August volumes), which is where fomo leaderboard traders' visible PnL concentrates.

findings.claim: Token lifecycle on Robinhood Chain is extremely short: across 13 days (Jul 16-28, 63.5M trades, 823,712 wallets) ~15,000 tokens launched per day, 84% never traded again after day one, the median new token had 13 trades, $1,200 volume and 4 participating wallets, and only 4-13% were still trading 48 hours later. Median trade size was $48.42; 3 of 4 open memecoin positions were underwater (median -27.7%); memecoin trade win rate 51.1% vs 19.3% on tokenized stocks.
findings.evidence: Bitquery investigation '63M trades inside Robinhood Chain' (Jul 16-28, 2026 dataset).
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Survival filters (e.g., still trading at 48h, >N unique wallets, graduated) prune >95% of launches. The $48 median trade size confirms a retail-dominated tape where a few-thousand-dollar order is 'whale-sized' relative to the median but small relative to graduated-pool depth.

findings.claim: Bot/HFT concentration on Robinhood Chain is extreme at the transaction level: one address submitted 25.0% of all trades and the top five addresses 70.2% of trade count in Jul 16-28; bot/HFT wallets were 1.7% of wallets but 51.3% of volume. However, measured genuine arbitrage profit was only ~$599K over 13 days (~$1 per $20,000 traded) and Bitquery found 'no evidence of widespread front-running'; HFT bots on stock tokens had only a 33.3% win rate.
findings.evidence: Bitquery investigation: 'Single largest address: submits 25.0% of all trades; Top 5 addresses combined: 70.2%'; 'Bot/HFT wallets: 1.7% of population, 51.3% of volume'; 'Genuine arbitrage total: $599,000 over 13 days'.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Volume/tx-count based signals (e.g., 'token X has 5,000 trades') are heavily polluted by a handful of bot addresses; dedupe by wallet and exclude the top ~5 addresses before using activity as a signal. Sandwich/MEV tax on retail appears low, so slippage settings can be tight-ish (limited by pool depth, not by MEV).

findings.claim: Transaction ordering: Robinhood Chain is an Arbitrum Orbit ('Arbitrum Dedicated Blockchain') L2 with a single Robinhood-operated sequencer, ~100 ms blocks, ~100 ms soft confirmations via Nitro preconfirmations, strict first-come-first-served ordering by arrival time at the sequencer, no public mempool, no Timeboost express lane (the express-lane bitmap is empty on the sequencer feed), and priority fees do not reorder transactions. Latency to the sequencer is therefore the only ordering lever.
findings.evidence: docs.robinhood.com/chain: 'first-come, first-served sequencing model, where the order is determined strictly by the arrival time at the sequencer'. Chainstack sequencer-feed repo: 'blockMetadata... is empty... Its absence here means no Timeboost: no express lane, no bidding your way to the front of a block'; ~71 tx/s. Chainstack 'what is Robinhood Chain': single sequencer operated by Robinhood, ~0.1 s blocks, soft confirmations ~100 ms, avg fee ~0.00002 ETH. docs.robinhood.com/chain/transaction-finality: soft confirmation sub-second, L1 posting minutes, finality ~13 min.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: There is no mempool to front-run and no gas auction to win; you cannot 'pay to jump the queue'. A retail user routed through fomo/Robinhood Wallet loses only on network path latency, not on fee bidding. Copy-trading a leader's on-chain tx is a race measured in tens of ms to the sequencer, which a phone app will lose to co-located bots but which matters little once outside the first few seconds of a launch.

findings.claim: A public sequencer feed exists (wss://feed.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com) that broadcasts ordering decisions with calldata before RPCs/indexers re-execute the block, giving a 'read, not race' head start over RPC/app feeds; bots decode selector/recipient/value cheaply and recover sender via ECDSA (~70 us/tx). BlockRazor benchmarked its regional RPC (Frankfurt/Ohio/Japan/Singapore) at 88-98% inclusion-rate success vs 2-12% for Robinhood's public RPC, which Robinhood itself says is 'not intended for production-grade... latency-sensitive applications'. Chain uptime was ~98% over 30 days in August with several state-update/data-submission interruptions (e.g., Aug 11 2h45m no state updates).
findings.evidence: Chainstack sequencer feed repo and search summary (endpoint wss://feed.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com); BlockRazor blog (inclusion-rate benchmark, official RPC disclaimer); status/uptime figures from Chainstack/statusgator search results.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: This is likely how fomoapi.io's '~15 s ahead of the app' on-chain feed works (sequencer feed vs fomo's app-side indexing). A retail-executable strategy should assume the sequencer feed is the true source of leader-trade signals and that the app feed lags; it also means the edge from 'seeing' a leader trade first is small in absolute ms but large versus the ~15 s app lag.

findings.claim: Gas is not negligible during congestion: chain fee revenue went from $56K on Aug 23 to $3.75M on Sep 1 (record, fourth straight record day), then $4.45M on Sep 2; peak individual gas prices hit ~0.027 ETH (~$64.53) per transaction, and one analysis put entry+exit gas at $20-30+ each for a $1,000 memecoin buy via aggregator, consuming ~12.5% of winning-trade profits. The 90-day Robinhood Wallet gas subsidy (threshold cut from $5 to $0.50 on Aug 8) ends Sep 29, 2026; fomo sponsors gas via ERC-4337 paymaster.
findings.evidence: Bitrue: peak gas 0.026944 ETH (~$64.53); $20+/$30+ examples; 12.54% of profits. Cryptonomist/CryptoTimes: $3.75M Sep 1, $4.45M Sep 2 fees. KuCoin: subsidy threshold cut to $0.50 on Aug 8, expires Sep 29; crypto.news: subsidy booked to Robinhood marketing, ends Sep 29. Datawallet (fomo): 'Network gas: Sponsored by Fomo'.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Post-Sep 29 unit economics change for Robinhood Wallet users (and may change for fomo if it stops sponsoring gas during spikes). Backtests on late-Aug/early-Sep data should add a congestion gas cost model; the FCFS design means congestion shows up as failed/delayed inclusion rather than fee bidding, which is a hidden execution risk for app users.

findings.claim: Chain-level scale (DefiLlama-sourced): DEX volume $989M on Aug 28, $1.49B on Aug 31/Sep 1 (2nd globally behind Solana), $1.595B Sep 1 and up to ~$1.89B reported; 7-day $7.25B, 30-day $17.75B; TVL $708-740M end-Aug; stablecoins ~$770-800M; 5.52M tx/day record Aug 30; DAU peaked 323,969 on Jul 21. Uniswap V3+V4 carried ~81% of DEX volume (v4 $720M = 51% of all Uniswap v4 volume globally). Memecoins were 79.2% of DEX volume in July and >80% by late August; Pons alone was ~51% of chain volume on Aug 30 ($445M of $874.8M).
findings.evidence: The Defiant Sep 1; The Block Aug 31; Datawallet stats; CoinGecko Learn (79.2% July); crypto.news (Pons 51% Aug 30); Cryptorank.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: The regime in your fomo leaderboard sample (Jul-Sep) is a blow-off growth phase: volume 3x'd in the last week of August. Leaderboard PnL is regime-conditional; expect mean reversion of both activity and unrealized PnL after the gas subsidy ends and if the PONS-buyback reflexivity breaks.

findings.claim: Retail order flow venues: on Sep 2 (Dune chart by analyst 'Adam'/adam_tehc, cross-checked with DefiLlama), trading terminals did $1.03B; GMGN $479.7M (91% of GMGN's global $490.9M settled on Robinhood Chain), fomo $268.2M, Axiom $95.5M, basedbot $77.8M, pump.fun app $67M. Chaincatcher cites GMGN ~17,700 daily active addresses (~$62.8K per address, pro/HFT profile) vs fomo >64,000 DAAs (~$1,565 per address, broad retail, ~40k new users/day) and Pons ~115,000 daily active wallets. GMGN+Pons+Uniswap produced ~88% of the chain's $2.66M app revenue on Aug 30 (GMGN $1.11M, Pons $930K, Uniswap $307K). fomo had 600K+ users, $4B+ cumulative volume and hit #3-#5 in US Finance app charts by Aug 21.
findings.evidence: bitcoinethereumnews (Dune/DefiLlama terminal table, Sep 2); Chaincatcher (per-app DAAs and per-address volume); Arkham research (app revenue split Aug 30); Bitcoin.com (fomo app-store rank, users, volume).
findings.relevance_to_strategy: fomo is the dominant small-ticket retail venue (~15% of chain DEX volume, by far the most wallets) while GMGN carries the pro/bot flow (~25-30% of volume). Leader trades on the fomo leaderboard are therefore a sample of the crowd, not of the sharpest money; GMGN-routed wallets are the ones more likely to be ahead of you. No published figure was found for Robinhood Wallet's own share of memecoin order flow (see open questions).

findings.claim: Fee/execution structure of the retail apps: fomo charges ~0.5% per spot trade with a $1 minimum (10% off with referral), sponsors gas via ERC-4337 paymaster, routes via DFlow for front-running protection and Relay for bridging, and offers social 'follow' rather than automated copy-trading; GMGN charges 1% per trade (plus launchpad fees), offers a launch sniper, copy-trading and anti-MEV on Solana, and recommends 30-50%+ slippage on new tokens.
findings.evidence: Datawallet fomo explainer (0.5%, paymaster, DFlow, Relay, no auto-copy); intercom fee guide (0.5%, $1 min); GMGN docs (1% fee, slippage guidance, sniper/copy features).
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Total explicit cost for a fomo user on a Pons V2 token: ~0.5% fomo + 1% Pons per side = ~3% round trip (plus creator tax if set). Because fomo has no auto-copy, the 'copy the leaderboard' behaviour is manual and slow (app lag ~15 s per fomoapi), which is exactly the latency a WebSocket-driven executor could beat.

findings.claim: Launchpad landscape and fee shares (Aug 31, per The Defiant/DefiLlama): Pons $4.89M (63.9% of ALL launchpad fees across chains; pump.fun 22.5%), Pons V1 $508K, NOXA Fun $143K, o1 Exchange $141K, LetsCash $48K, Pools.trade $39K. NOXA (live Jun 16, 1% swap fee, ~18,600 launches/day, ~60K tokens, $12M fees) halted launches Jul 11 citing bot spam/copycats and later redirected 100% of fees to creators; Pons launched Jul 13 and absorbed the category. Uniswap Labs' Pools.trade (Aug 5) has zero launch fee and a 0.25% autocompounding LP fee (creator optional 0.05%), Crowd Launch (4-hour TWAP window, $10K FDV min) or Instant Launch (curve), creator buy forced into the launch block; it out-launched Pons on day one (10,506 vs 7,210) but fees fell 86% within a week. LONG (long.xyz) pairs memecoins against tokenized stocks (AI/NVDA, BONER/HIMS, SPACEHOOD/SPCX), $151M volume Sep 1 (#2 launchpad by volume). Others: o1.exchange (1% terminal fee), ArrowPad (curve, 1% fee, auto-graduate to Uniswap), hood.fun, Flap, Klik, LetsCash (CASHCAT community v4 launchpad), PAIR (multipool RWA launchpad, Aug 31), hoodr aggregator.
findings.evidence: The Defiant Sep 1 and Aug 12 pieces; CoinGecko Learn (NOXA 65.8% of tokens Jun 30-Jul 11, ~60K tokens); Uniswap blog and The Defiant (Pools.trade mechanics/day-one numbers); Cryptorank (long.xyz $151.4M); MEXC Learn on Long.xyz; Bitrue launchpad roundup; search snippets for ArrowPad/hood.fun/o1.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Pons is ~60-80% of launches and the majority of fees; a Pons-only model covers most of the fomo Robinhood feed. Pools.trade tokens (0.25% fee, deeper autocompounding liquidity) and LONG stock-paired tokens (quoted in NVDA/HIMS etc., not ETH) are different microstructures that need separate handling — especially LONG pairs, whose price depends on the stock-token peg (HIMS traded at a 4.6x premium; BONER cornered 53% of HIMS token supply).

findings.claim: Liquidity vs headline market cap is thin: CASHCAT had ~$6.6M liquidity at a $150M market cap; PONS had ~$1.03M in its main WETH pool at a $26.5M FDV (Jul 21); FRONG $1.1M liquidity at $12.1M FDV; PIPEDOG ~$4.5M ETH liquidity at ~$30M market cap; TENDIES showed two-sided depth only in the 'low tens of thousands of dollars at the 2% level' with ~$20M market cap; Artificial Inu had ~$3.3M in its NVDA pool (3x its WETH pool). Every V2 graduation seeds a pool of identical size (from the 4.2 ETH curve proceeds less the reserved allocation), i.e. roughly $10K-order liquidity at graduation.
findings.evidence: Bitcoin.com/Lookonchain (CASHCAT $6.6M liq vs $150M); KuCoin PONS guide ($1.03M vs $26.5M FDV); The Defiant (FRONG); Odaily/0xSun (PIPEDOG); KuCoin TENDIES article; The Block (AI/NVDA pool). Pons V2 search summary: 'every launch on the same settings graduates into a pool of the same size, at the same price'.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Liquidity/market-cap ratios of ~2-5% mean 'PnL' on fomo leaderboards (mark-to-market) is largely unrealizable for large holders; a $10K sell into a $20K-depth pool is a double-digit-% price impact. Size strategies to pool depth (read V3/V4 pool reserves), not to market cap, and treat leaderboard unrealized PnL as a noisy signal of skill.

findings.claim: Bundling/insider concentration is common on the biggest runners: PIPEDOG (Jul 28, 140x to ~$74M within hours) had one entity controlling ~50% via ~80 fresh CEX-funded wallets that sniped 54% at launch ($1M sold, $16M still held); ARROW had 80% of supply in ~200 wallets funded from one source and sniped within 3 minutes, later down >95%; VLAD (launched off Vlad Tenev's hacked X account) was ~70% bundled; CASHDOG heavily bundled. By contrast CASHCAT and TENDIES had clean distributions. Bubblemaps found 63% of 164,538 traders across the top-50 Robinhood memecoins lost money (37% profitable); a similar community estimate is 65/35.
findings.evidence: Bubblemaps blog posts ('Robinhood trenches, $11M gone, and 164k traders later'; 'Onchain insights: CATE... 29 wallets'); Cryptopolitan summary; CryptoTimes (PIPEDOG price path); Bitquery/Hackernoon 35%/65% estimate.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: A cheap on-chain feature (share of supply bought in first N blocks by fresh wallets funded from a common source) separates 'clean' runners from bundled ones; bundled runners can still run hard (PIPEDOG) but carry a known overhang. Bubblemaps V2 supports Robinhood Chain in beta if you want a labeled dataset.

findings.claim: Notable runners and drivers: CASHCAT (deployed on NOXA pre-mainnet; named after Robinhood's original 'CashCat' name) went 1,700%+ in 24h and 2,100% in week one to ~$156M (Jul 8-12), fell 33% after NOXA's exit, then re-rallied 120% in early Aug on the official Robinhood listing (Aug 6) with Bubblemaps flagging fresh-wallet accumulation two days before the listing and a $1M single buy on Aug 2; peaked ~$250M Aug 27; early wallets turned $838 into ~$1.05M (1,250x) and $85 into ~$2.5M unrealized. PONS went from ~$0.0033 (Jul 17) to ~$0.60 (Sep 3, ~181x; market cap $300-576M depending on tracker), driven by the 80%-of-protocol-fees buyback-and-burn (~29% of supply burned), Pons fee records ($5.34M Aug 30, $5.95M Sep 1-3), a Gate.io listing (~Aug 27) and Binance Wallet Alpha (Sep 2); it crashed ~49% the week Pools.trade launched (Aug 5). Artificial Inu (AI, via LONG, paired with NVDA) rose from $1.5M (Aug 1) to $135M (Aug 30) and $250-320M in early Sep, catalyzed by an Aster DEX 5x-leverage listing (+70% in 24h). Other August runners: DELTA ($2M on Aug 24 -> $38M -> $18M), HMM ($7M -> $39M -> $21M), microduck ($20M), YOLO ($12M), BONER/HIMS ($53M), SPACEHOOD ($16M), Biscotti ($10M in hours), TENDIES (~$20M, ATH mid-July), HOODRAT ($500K -> $5M after Matt Furie attention), UP, NetNet.
findings.evidence: crypto.news CASHCAT explainer; KuCoin CASHCAT profit post; Bubblemaps; Decrypt PONS piece; The Defiant Sep 1; Morning Minute Aug 27 (Gate.io listing, ATHs); KuCoin token overview Sep 2; The Block Aug 31; Ambcrypto/Kucoin AI coverage; Odaily 0xSun.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: The largest moves were catalyst-driven (CEX/Robinhood listings, perp listings on Hyperliquid/Aster, protocol buybacks, celebrity attention), not launch-sniping. A catalyst-anticipation strategy on already-graduated, liquid tokens (top-20 by liquidity) has a plausible, retail-executable edge; the July 'chain launch' regime (pre-mainnet NOXA deployments) is unrepeatable.

findings.claim: VOXEL and MANCER are not memecoins in the usual sense. VOXEL is the token of Voxelithic Protocol, a zero-fee (30 bps ceiling in-contract) liquidity router on Robinhood Chain reading 60 pools across 6 venues (Uniswap v3/v4, Ramses, Giga, Up, Alandale) that converts everything it receives into VOXEL and burns it; it went live Sep 1, 2026 and is unaudited. MANCER is the token of Mancer, a DEX aggregator/limit-order hub ('Jupiter of Robinhood Chain') by Michael Hirsch ('The SlopFather') with Clutch Markets, launched with a 5,000-piece Chain Mancers NFT collection, 2.5B supply, >$465K fills on day one. Both are 'infrastructure narrative' tokens that led the late-August rotation from pure memes to utility/infra (Delta, UP, NetNet, Mancer, PONS).
findings.evidence: voxelithic.xyz site and Voxelithic X account (via search); The Bored Ape Gazette and eGamers on Mancer; MEXC tokenomics (2.5B supply); The Block Aug 31 on rotation to utility tokens.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: If fomo leaderboard leaders' late-August gains cluster in VOXEL/MANCER/DELTA/PONS, their edge was narrative rotation into 'fee-burn infra' tokens, a theme trade rather than launch sniping — replicable with a theme screen but with concentration risk (unaudited contracts, reflexive burn narratives).

findings.claim: Stock-paired memecoins (via LONG and Pons V2 custom pairs) became a distinct, larger-than-RWA layer: on Sep 2 memecoin-pair volume using stock tokens was $217M vs $127M direct stock-token trading; 432 stock-paired pools held ~$8.84M of stock tokens and did $95.3M/24h; stock-paired memecoins were ~25% of stock-linked volume. Fake tickers are rampant: 361 contracts claimed 'GME', 354 impostors did $213M volume (2x the real one), 64,394 wallets bought fakes with median loss -52.4%.
findings.evidence: Cryptoslate Sep 2; KuCoin stock-paired piece; The Block Aug 31; Bitquery investigation (fake-ticker stats).
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Ticker-string matching is unsafe on this chain; key everything by contract address. Stock-paired pools have quote-asset risk (stock-token premium/mint gaps around NYSE hours) that ETH-paired models do not capture.

findings.claim: Robinhood's own economics/positioning: Robinhood earns 'a few basis points per transaction' on the chain with ~half shared with Arbitrum (Q2 call), 90% of sequencer revenue retained / 8% Arbitrum DAO / 2% dev guild under the Arbitrum Expansion Program; Q2 2026 brokerage crypto revenue was $100M (-38% YoY) while the chain did >$47B cumulative DEX volume by mid-August. Robinhood listed CASHCAT on the brokerage (Aug 6), Robinhood Wallet added Crossmint credit-card (Apple/Google Pay) memecoin buys in August under MCC 5815, and Tenev said the chain 'works great for memes, too'. No source discloses Robinhood Wallet's share of on-chain memecoin order flow.
findings.evidence: Motley Fool Q2 2026 call transcript; SEC 8-K Q2 exhibit; crypto.news revenue-share; The Block credit-card story; Fortune Jul 13 Tenev quote.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Robinhood is economically aligned with memecoin volume (sequencer fees) and has shown it will list chain-native tokens on the brokerage; 'Robinhood listing' is a recurring, front-runnable catalyst (CASHCAT +100-120% on listing, with pre-listing accumulation flagged on-chain).

findings.claim: Speculative/low confidence: the Chaincatcher claim that fomo is '36% of Robinhood Chain trading volume' conflicts with Dune/DefiLlama terminal data (fomo $268M on a ~$1.6-1.9B day, i.e. ~15%); the 36% figure likely refers to fomo's share of terminal volume or of wallets, not chain DEX volume. Similarly, DefiLlama's fomo figure for Sep 2 ($27.2M) diverges 10x from the Dune figure ($268.2M), suggesting DefiLlama's fomo adapter undercounts Robinhood Chain.
findings.evidence: Chaincatcher: 'Fomo's daily trading volume: approximately $101 million (36% share)'; bitcoinethereumnews: Dune fomo $268.2M vs DefiLlama fomo $27.2M on Sep 2.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: When sizing how much of the tape the fomo feed 'sees', use the Dune terminal numbers (~15% of chain DEX volume, ~60K+ wallets/day) rather than either the 36% or the DefiLlama figure; fomo is the majority of small-ticket wallets but a minority of dollars.

open_questions: Exact Pons V2 curve parameters (phantom quote reserve size, reserved allocation %, opening market cap in ETH, pool size/price at graduation) are configurable per launch and not published in prose; read them from the factory/TokenLaunched events or the ponslaunchpad.com per-token pages and verify how many launches use non-default thresholds or creator taxes.

No public source quantifies Robinhood Wallet's share of memecoin order flow on Robinhood Chain (vs fomo/GMGN/Uniswap UI). Robinhood has not disclosed Wallet DAUs or swap volume; a router/aggregator-contract attribution on Dune (adam_tehc/the-robinhood-trenches) would be needed.

What fraction of Pons V2 launches use the up-to-32-address snipe-tax exemption list, and how much of graduated-token supply those exempt wallets hold at graduation (this is the structural 'bundling' channel in V2).

Whether fomo routes Robinhood Chain orders through DFlow/private relay or directly to the public sequencer, and whether fomo continues sponsoring gas during $60+/tx congestion spikes; also fomo's exact slippage defaults on Robinhood Chain.
Post-graduation performance distribution for V2 tokens (Aug 4-Sep 3): share reaching $1M/$5M/$20M, time-to-peak, and drawdown from peak; only a July V1 snapshot (529 grads, 1 above $5M) was found.

How the sequencer feed's ~15 s lead over the fomo app feed decomposes (app indexing lag vs network), and whether fomoapi.io's on-chain feed is derived from the public wss://feed.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com relay.
Whether the Sept 29 end of Robinhood's gas subsidy materially reduces retail flow (and thus leaderboard turnover) in October 2026; several sources flag this as the key regime-change risk.

CoinDesk articles (Jul 13, Jul 15, Aug 31, Sep 3) were rate-limited during this research; their figures here come from search snippets and syndications (cryptonews.net, Arkham) and should be re-verified against the originals.

findings.claim: Only ~6% of Fomo wallets were profitable on a realized basis over a 90-day window (DWF Ventures study, Aug 2026): 6.16% of ~292,000 wallets; only 25 wallets netted >$10k realized; aggregate losses estimated at ~$1.26B. DWF attributes losses to 'execution asymmetry' (followers fill later and worse) and an 'exit liquidity' loop where callers benefit from follower buying then sell into it.
findings.evidence: Yellow.com and AlexaBlockchain report the DWF Ventures study (published ~Aug 28, 2026): 292k wallets, 3 months, 6.16% profitable, 25 wallets >$10k net realized profit, measured on realized gains. Cointribune's version of the same story cites 304,161 active Solana DEX wallets, 19,003 profitable (6.25%), median loss $120, 88% of winners made <$100, $1.26B group losses. The two write-ups disagree slightly on sample definition (Fomo wallets vs Solana DEX wallets) - the underlying DWF post was not directly retrievable.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Directly on-platform base rate: naive copy-following on fomo is a ~94% losing proposition on realized PnL. Any strategy must beat this by avoiding late fills and by not being the caller's exit liquidity. Also confirms realized (not mark-to-market) PnL is the right metric for evaluating leaderboard traders.

findings.claim: Copy trading on a bonding curve carries a mechanical 'imitation penalty': even an instantaneous copier trades at a worse point on the curve than the leader, and adversarial bots (front-running, hidden positions, fabricated sentiment) systematically extract value from copiers. A defensive multi-agent filter still only reached ~3% average copier return per position after frictions.
findings.evidence: Luo, Feng, Xu, Liu (arXiv 2601.08641, Jan 2026) formalize leader vs one-to-one copier returns under the pump.fun bonding-curve model, coining the 'imitation penalty'. Data: 4,000 projects for development, 1,000 for evaluation, 614,330 wallet-coin pairs. Wallet-evaluation agent precision 70% (4,773 TP / 6,879 predicted); meme-evaluation F1 ~0.62 at 1h post-migration; selected KOL wallets earned ~$500k across projects; their system yields 'an average copier return of 3% per meme coin investment under realistic market frictions'. Paper also notes KOLs may pre-buy from a hidden wallet before the public wallet buys, and use copiers as exit liquidity.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Even a 15s-ahead on-chain feed cannot eliminate the structural curve penalty; edge from copying must come from selecting which leaders/positions to copy and from exiting before the leader, not from latency alone. The ~3% per-trade net return figure is a realistic ceiling for filtered copy strategies.

findings.claim: Pump.fun graduation rates are tiny and have declined: 0.63% (Sep-Oct 2025, 655,770 tokens, 4,338 graduated) and 0.20-0.21% (May-Jun 2026, 832,941 launches, 1,651 graduations within a ~6-minute observation window). Earlier peaks were ~2.1% (Jun 2024) and 1.67% (best week Nov 2024), falling below 1% by Feb-Mar 2025.
findings.evidence: Marino, Naviglio, Tarantelli, Lillo (arXiv 2602.14860): 655,770 tokens, 243,123 creators, 2.6M traders, 4,338 graduated (~0.63%). Kamat (arXiv 2607.02823, RED-PUMP-2026-v1): 832,941 launches May 8-Jun 10 2026, fast-regime graduation 0.198% (CI 0.189-0.208%), steady-state 0.207%; note the collector only observes ~6 minutes post-launch so this is a lower bound. The Block (Feb 2025): 2.1% in Jun 2024, 1.6% Jan 2025, 0.7% early Feb 2025. Cointelegraph (Mar 2025): 1.67% best week Nov 2024, <1% Feb 17-Mar 14 2025.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Buying pre-graduation on a bonding-curve launchpad is a lottery with <1% hit rate; a naive buy-and-hold at any curve level sits below breakeven (see Marino et al.). Any launch-stage strategy needs strong conditioning signals or must avoid the pre-graduation phase entirely.

findings.claim: On pump.fun, baseline graduation probability sits below the naive buy-and-hold breakeven curve over most of the curve; the strongest predictors of graduation are liquidity velocity (reaching a given SOL level in very few trades), a high non-bot share of trades, and (weakly) early participation by ex-ante identified top traders. 92% of tokens with >=30 swaps show at least one dump event.
findings.evidence: Marino et al. (arXiv 2602.14860, Feb 2026): breakeven for buy-and-hold to graduation is P(grad|vSol) > vSol^2/115^2 (ignoring fees); baseline probability 'remains below the economic breakeven over most of the vSol range'; only conditioning on non-bot share >=0.7 approaches breakeven near the threshold. Tokens reaching a vSol level with <=10 trades graduate far more often. Top traders identified in weeks 1-2 and tested out-of-sample on weeks 3-4: conditional graduation probability above baseline but 'modest and non-monotonic'. Of 184,282 tokens with >=30 swaps, 169,938 (92.22%) exhibit >=1 dump (log-return < -4 sigma). Selling before graduation yields higher proceeds than after due to the liquidity structure.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Provides tested conditioning variables: trade-count-per-SOL (velocity), bot share, and top-trader presence. The out-of-sample 'top trader presence' effect is real but small - directly relevant to whether fomo leaderboard presence in a token is a usable signal.

findings.claim: Off-chain social presence at launch is a strong graduation predictor: pump.fun launches advertising a Telegram channel graduate at 1.485% vs 0.166% without (8.94x lift, Cox HR 5.40); launches with all three social channels graduate at 1.919% vs 0.110% with none (17.4x). Higher initial market cap also predicts graduation (top quartile >31.04 SOL: 0.634%; HR 4.51 per log unit). Median time-to-graduation for fast graduators was 1.66 min.
findings.evidence: Kamat, arXiv 2607.02823 (Jun 2026, v2 Aug 2026), 832,941 launches, 1,651 graduations, Harrell's concordance 0.858. Note: only the first ~6 minutes are observed, so results describe the 'fast regime'.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Cheap, immediately available launch metadata (socials, initial buy size) is a large-magnitude filter. Worth testing analogous filters on Pons/Robinhood Chain launches (does the token have socials, how big is the creator's initial buy).

findings.claim: Most graduated pump.fun tokens collapse almost immediately after migration: 73% fall below 40% of their migration price within 20 minutes; 60.3% drop 80%+ in that window. 84% of 41,470 migrated tokens (Dec 2024-Mar 2025) were classified high-risk; bundled/coordinated accounts held 36.5% of supply on average. ML filtering (MLP, precision 0.85 for high-risk) cut simulated losses from >60% (random picks) to 26.6% (top-100 picks).
findings.evidence: MemeTrans / MELT dataset, Hu et al., Georgia Tech, arXiv 2602.13480 (Feb 2026): 41,470 migrated launches, 218.5M transactions; high-risk 84.13%, medium 11.34%, low 4.53%; min_price_ratio<0.2 for 60.26%; bundle identification raised top-10 holder share by 24% for high-risk tokens; AUPRC 0.573, F1 0.698; a TCN detects post-migration price/volume manipulation at 87.85% accuracy on 1,555 labeled tokens (599 manipulated).
findings.relevance_to_strategy: The migration event is the key sell point, not a buy point: post-graduation buyers are the exit liquidity for curve buyers. Holder-concentration / bundle features at migration are strongly predictive of collapse and can be computed on-chain before entry.

findings.claim: Realized-profit distribution on pump.fun is extremely skewed: as of Jan 2025, of 13.4M wallets only 0.4% (55,012) realized >$10k, 0.048% (~6,432) >$100k, and 0.002% (294) >$1M. Monthly share of profitable traders was below 50% most months from Apr 2024 to late 2025 (low of 30.1% in Jun 2025), then rose to 56.8% (Feb 2026), 70.0% (Mar 2026), 73.3% (Apr 2026) as the active-wallet base shrank from 5.2M (May 2025) to 1.8M (Dec 2025) and became more selective.
findings.evidence: Decrypt (Jan 10, 2025) citing Dune researcher Adam Tehc; CoinGecko Research (May 7, 2026) 'Pump.fun Traders Are Making a Comeback' using Dune realized-PnL data (excludes never-sold holders; acknowledges bot inflation and illiquid pricing). In Apr 2026, 65.1% of profitable wallets (2.05M) made $1-$500; 5.4% (169k) >$1,000.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Profitability is regime- and crowd-dependent: when tourists leave, remaining (more sophisticated) traders' win rates rise. A sustainable strategy should be evaluated across regimes; median profitable wallet earns only hundreds of dollars a month, so 'retail-executable' expectations must be modest.

findings.claim: Deployer-funded same-block sniping on pump.fun is a persistent, highly profitable insider tactic: 15,000+ launches in ~1 month (Mar 15-Jun 2025) were sniped in the creation block by wallets funded directly by the deployer; 4,600+ sniper wallets and 10,400+ deployers; >15,000 SOL realized net profit; 87% of snipes profitable; 55% sold within 1 minute, 85% within 5 minutes, 11% within 15 seconds; >90% exit in 1-2 sells; activity concentrated 14:00-23:00 UTC and nearly dormant 00:00-08:00 UTC.
findings.evidence: Pine Analytics report (Jun 9, 2025) as reported by BeInCrypto/Bitget and ChainCatcher; ~1.75% of pump.fun launch activity. Per-wallet gains typically 1-100 SOL, some >500 SOL.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Insider snipers are a documented persistent edge, but it is unavailable to retail (requires deployer collusion). For a retail strategy this is a filter: tokens where the first-block buyer is deployer-funded will be dumped within ~1-5 minutes. Also gives a time-of-day prior (insider activity peaks US hours).

findings.claim: Coordinated wallet cohorts snipe launches at scale on pump.fun: 1,012 persistent cohorts (2-12 wallets, 2,965 addresses) were detected across 166,098 launches over 13.4 days (Jun 11-25, 2026); 7.0% of cohort-treated launches had zero non-cohort buyers in the first 30 minutes; cohort presence lifts first-30-min buyer counts by +16.1% (95% CI 13.0-19.4%) but SOL inflow lift is indistinguishable from zero (+6.3%, CI -0.5 to +15.1%).
findings.evidence: Kamat, arXiv 2607.02795 (Aug 2026), RED-COHORT-2026-v1 on Zenodo; 1,578,333 buyer observations; propensity-score-matched. Profitability of cohorts not reported in the abstract; full text not retrievable here.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Early 'buyer count' surges are partly manufactured by cohorts and do not translate into real SOL inflow - so buyer-count momentum signals in the first 30 minutes are contaminated. Use SOL/ETH net inflow rather than wallet counts as the momentum proxy.

findings.claim: Independent sniping (non-insider) is, on average, unprofitable on Ethereum: the average sniper in a snipe bundle loses money due to builder bribes; only the lead sniper is sometimes profitable and at the expense of other snipers. On Solana, majority of launches are sniped in-block, and industry benchmarks claim only ~10% of sniper bots are consistently profitable (unverified vendor claim).
findings.evidence: Gigabots 'Sniping Sucks' (Medium) profitability analysis of average vs lead sniper (content behind 403 here; summary from search index). Academic: 'Ready, Aim, Snipe!' (WWW 2023 companion) and 'The Blockchain Warfare: Investigating the Ecosystem of Sniper Bots' (ACM 2025) exist but full text was not retrievable (403). Vendor claims (rpcfast, velvosoft) that >50% of pump.fun tokens are sniped in the creation block and only ~10% of bots profit are unsourced.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Competing as a latency sniper is negative-sum for non-insiders; the fomoapi 15s-ahead feed does not make one a sniper. Do not build the strategy around being first-in-block.

findings.claim: Rug/soft-rug base rates are extreme: Solidus Labs' 2025 report found 98.6% of ~7M pump.fun tokens (Jan 2024-Mar 2025, >=5 trades) fell below $1,000 liquidity (only ~97k retained >$1k); 93% of 388k Raydium pools showed soft-rug (>=90% liquidity removal) characteristics; median rug size ~$2,832, 25% under $732. Chainalysis found 3.59-4.5% of 3M+ tokens launched in 2024 showed pump-and-dump traits and ~89-94% of suspicious pools were rugged by the pool creator (or creator-funded addresses).
findings.evidence: Solidus Labs report page and CoinDesk coverage (May 2025) - note the $1k liquidity threshold measures collapse, not proven fraud. Chainalysis 2025 Crypto Crime Report as summarized by crypto.news and cryptopotato: 74,037 tokens (3.59%), only 1.7% of 2024 tokens still actively traded 30 days later; $2.57B wash volume across ETH/BNB/Base.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Nearly all launchpad tokens go to ~zero; 'survival' and creator-linked wallet behavior are the dominant risk variables. Median rug sizes are small, implying the typical token never had meaningful liquidity - position sizing must assume near-total loss on most positions.

findings.claim: Bots dominate launchpad order flow: Trading-Operations bots concentrate >80% of their transactions in the pump.fun ecosystem; bot-related DEX transactions exceeded $250M/day in Jan 2026; industry estimates put bots at 60-80% of pump.fun token volume (unverified). Solana MEV/arb bot success depends heavily on venue (62.3% of HumidiFi-invoking txs profitable vs 21.0% otherwise).
findings.evidence: Zheng et al., 'Demystifying Solana Bots' (ASE 2026, arXiv 2607.28424): 586 GitHub bot repos, 200 on-chain bot addresses, 44.1M transactions. The 60-80% volume-share figure comes from DEXTools/BeInCrypto articles without a stated methodology.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Volume and transaction-count signals on new tokens are largely bot-generated; strategies should discount raw volume and weight unique-funded-wallet net inflow. Marino et al.'s non-bot-share variable is the tested version of this idea.

findings.claim: On the fomo/Solana copy-trading population, the hazard is not just latency: DWF frames a structural feedback loop where public callers build reputations from calls that become partly self-fulfilling as followers buy, and followers 'absorb the drop when the caller sells'. Multiple documented cases show KOL/insider dumps: SHAR (insider sold 50% of supply for ~19,620 SOL ~$3.38M; KOLs deleted promo tweets), YZY (73.87% of buyers lost), HAWK (285 wallets held 96%), WOLF (insiders 82%, -99% in 2 days).
findings.evidence: DWF study coverage (Yellow, AlexaBlockchain); Cryptotimes on SHAR (Oct 2024); Bubblemaps-derived YZY figure via search summary; Chainalysis/coinlaw coverage of HAWK and WOLF.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: On a social trading app, the leaderboard/caller effect is itself a manipulation vector: the profitable side of the trade is being the caller (or exiting before the caller). Strategy should detect caller sells (on-chain, ~15s early via fomoapi) and treat them as hard exit signals.

findings.claim: Crowd-sourced explicit trading signals from X/Reddit/Stocktwits/Telegram do carry short-horizon predictive power, strongest for low-market-cap assets and assets with recent negative returns (28,000+ LLM-extracted signals).
findings.evidence: 'Wisdom of the crowd signals: Predictive power of social media trading signals' (Electronic Markets, 2025, Springer). Full text was paywalled here; magnitude, horizon, and after-cost profitability not verified.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Supports the idea that fomo feed 'calls' contain information for low-cap tokens over short horizons, but the DWF result shows the same signals lose money for followers in practice - the difference is execution timing and who exits first.

findings.claim: General crypto intraday evidence shows both intraday momentum (late-informed investors) and intraday reversal (overreaction); at the memecoin level, established memecoins show volatility tightly coupled to bursts of activity and short-cycle inflows, with top-100 holder concentration typically >70% (TRUMP/LIBRA/MELANIA >98%), which magnifies both spikes and reversals. No peer-reviewed study was found quantifying minute-level momentum vs reversal specifically for sub-$1M-cap launchpad tokens.
findings.evidence: ScienceDirect 'Intraday return predictability in the cryptocurrency markets' (NAJEF, 2022) - abstract only; Xiang et al. 'Measuring Memecoin Fragility' (arXiv 2512.00377, Nov 2025) ME2F framework with VDS/WDS/SAS scores. The closest low-cap microstructure evidence is MemeTrans' 20-minute post-migration collapse statistics and Marino's dump clustering at specific vSol levels.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: There is no published minute-level momentum/reversal study for launchpad tokens - this is a gap the team's own backtest on fomo/Pons data would have to fill. Prior evidence leans toward sharp mean reversion (collapse) after early spikes, with momentum only where real (non-bot) inflow continues.

findings.claim: Robinhood Chain launchpad activity is very large and highly concentrated: on Aug 29, 2026, 23,080 tokens were deployed on Robinhood Chain, 15,957 (69.1%) via Pons V2 (Flap 2,109; Long 1,805; Bankr 1,534; Trenched.today 833); Pons reported 124,016 launches with 1,362 graduated (~1.1%) and ~$116M volume / 1.68M trades / ~98k wallets in its first weeks; ten wallets minted a quarter of tokens; Pons collected ~$4.89M daily fees on Aug 31, 2026 (~63.9% of tracked launchpad fees). Pons V2 (Aug 2026) integrates Uniswap V4 hooks with dynamic fees and tokenized-stock pairs.
findings.evidence: KuCoin flash (Aug 30, 2026, citing Dune via Odaily); search-index summaries of MEXC/KuCoin/TrustSwap articles; cryptonews.net on Pons V2 Uniswap V4 integration. TrustSwap's guide describes Pons as a 'pump.fun-style bonding curve' with graduation to a DEX pool - this conflicts with the parent's established fact that Pons has no bonding curve and a Uniswap V3 pool from launch; may reflect V1 vs V2 or third-party error.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Robinhood Chain now mirrors pump.fun's structure (tens of thousands of launches/day, ~1% graduation, creator concentration), so pump.fun base rates are a reasonable prior. The Uniswap V4 dynamic-fee/hook mechanics of Pons V2 and the 2-block launch protection need on-chain verification before any sniping/entry-timing assumptions.

findings.claim: fomo's own copy-trading docs and FAQ make no profitability claims; the docs page describes copy trading for Hyperliquid addresses (market entry 'immediately at current market price', multipliers 0.5x-5x, threshold filters), with disclaimers that 'many copy traders experience periods of losses' and that '10-20% monthly returns are exceptional, not typical'.
findings.evidence: docs.onfomo.com/trading/copy and fomo.family/answers/how-profitable-is-copy-trading fetched directly.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: No platform-published follower-outcome data; the DWF study is the only external measurement. Also note the copy-trade doc found describes Hyperliquid perps copying, not memecoin spot - memecoin 'copying' on fomo is manual feed-following, which worsens execution asymmetry.

findings.claim: Search-index text attributed an 'early-buyer' study to 'Jarek Hirniak, University of Warsaw' (200,000+ bonding-curve tokens; <0.5% of tokens positive for buyers entering after the first 10% of supply). This could not be verified against any primary source and should be treated as unconfirmed/possibly spurious.
findings.evidence: Appeared only in a search-engine synthesized summary; no URL, paper, or author page located before the search budget was exhausted.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Do not cite. The verifiable analogue is Marino et al.'s breakeven analysis (buy-and-hold below breakeven over most of the curve) and MemeTrans' post-migration collapse rates.

open_questions: What does the full text of Kamat's sniper-cohort paper (arXiv 2607.02795) report on cohort PnL and exit timing? (PDF text was not extractable; the HTML version 404s.)
What are the magnitude/horizon/after-cost results in 'Wisdom of the crowd signals' (Electronic Markets 2025) for low-cap tokens? Paywalled.
DWF Ventures' original post: is the 292k-wallet sample fomo-only or all Solana DEX wallets (cointribune cites 304,161)? How were 'Fomo wallets' identified, and was PnL realized-only?

Pons mechanics conflict: third-party guides describe a pump.fun-style bonding curve with graduation, while the established facts say no bonding curve and a Uniswap V3 pool from launch (V2 now cites Uniswap V4 hooks + dynamic fees). Needs on-chain verification, including the 2-block launch protection and whether deployer-funded same-block sniping is feasible on Robinhood Chain.

No peer-reviewed minute-level momentum vs reversal study exists for sub-$1M launchpad tokens; the team's own backtest on fomo/Pons trade data is required. Suggested tested conditioning variables from the literature: non-bot share, trade-count-per-unit-inflow (velocity), unique-funded-wallet net inflow (not buyer counts), bundle/top-10 holder share at migration, social-link presence at launch, and caller/leader sell events.
Are there published post-graduation return curves (e.g., 1h/24h/7d) for pump.fun or Pons graduates beyond MemeTrans' 20-minute window? None found with a citable source.

Is there quantitative evidence on KOL-wallet aggregate realized PnL (e.g., Kolscan/Bubblemaps datasets) showing what share of tracked KOLs are net profitable? Not reached before search budget was exhausted.

findings.claim: CROSS-CUTTING: fomo's leaderboard PnL is mark-to-market on holdings and is publicly criticized as inflated; an X analyst (MidCurveMortal, 2026-08-31) claims unipcs's price-impact-adjusted PnL is only ~25% of the displayed figure, and that fomo advertises 'ALL holdings as profit on INFINITE liquidity'. Independent coverage (TronWeekly/Arkham) stresses the same: 'a displayed portfolio gain is not the same as realized profit'.
findings.evidence: KuCoin-syndicated post: 'FOMO app KOL unipcs price-impact adjusted PNL is only 25% of what is flaunted... advertising ALL holdings as profit on INFINITE liquidity' (single-source, no methodology shown). TronWeekly on Bonk Guy's $14.5M fomo portfolio: unrealized; 'thin liquidity can make positions difficult to sell without moving prices'. BTCC: >$1M unrealized PnL needed to enter fomo's 30d top-30; 25 users >$1M in 30d. fomo's own leaderboard explainer never defines realized vs unrealized. Local leaderboard JSON confirms volumeUsd is identical across 24h/7d/30d/all windows (i.e., cumulative), so PnL/volume ratios can be computed per trader.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Leaderboard rank is a poor proxy for extractable edge; any copy/follow strategy must re-score traders on realized, price-impact-adjusted PnL and discount concentrated illiquid bags.

findings.claim: CROSS-CUTTING: Several top-ranked handles show PnL that is orders of magnitude larger than their cumulative fomo trade volume, which is only possible if the PnL is unrealized appreciation on cheap early buys and/or on tokens acquired outside fomo (transferred into the linked wallets). Ratios (all-time PnL / cumulative volume from local fomoapi leaderboards): Natan_benish 5.24M/12.6K (~415x, 1,891 trades = ~$7 avg trade), frogmanhaha 3.68M/21.9K (~168x, EVM-only wallet, 227 trades), ogle 2.93M/310K (~9x), DumbCrayonEater 9.35M/1.01M (~9x), unipcs 12.3M/2.36M (~5x). By contrast high-churn traders realize most PnL: frankdegods 2.58M/48.6M (0.05x), smol_intern 1.01M/12.9M (0.08x), change 3.40M/27.4M (0.12x), Aurelius0121 1.21M/8.5M (0.14x), ether_monk 2.77M/9.68M (0.29x), notanicecat69 3.05M/6.5M (0.47x).
findings.evidence: Computed from /home/user/fomo-memebot/data/raw/fomoapi/leaderboards/{24h,7d,30d,all}.json fields pnlUsd, volumeUsd, trades, holdings, wallets. volumeUsd and trades are identical in every window for each handle, so they are cumulative not per-window.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Separates 'bag-holders whose bag pumped' (unrealized, non-replicable) from 'active traders with realized churn' (the only cohort whose entries are even in principle copyable). Extreme ratios (Natan_benish, frogmanhaha) are red flags for wallet-funded-elsewhere PnL and should be excluded from copy universes.

findings.claim: unipcs (@theunipcs, 'Bonk Guy'): #1 on all four fomo leaderboards (24h $5.07M, 7d $10.4M, 30d $12.3M, all $12.3M; 465.8K fomo followers, 109 holdings). Major Solana memecoin KOL (public BONK $16k->$20M+, WIF, FARTCOIN, PNUT, POPCAT trades; a fan token 'BONK GUY WAS RIGHT' exists). On Robinhood Chain he holds ~1% of PONS supply (bought ~$67K USDG for 10.96M PONS at ~$6M mcap), ~2% of MARSCOIN, plus USELESS; Arkham valued the fomo portfolio at $14.5M on 2026-09-03 with $4.4M attributed to PONS. Style: concentrated conviction holds + public narrative calls to a large audience; he also 'calls' coins on X (e.g., $JUGGERNAUT, $USELESS as 'the DOGE/SHIB of this cycle'). He explicitly says fomo is his 'degen wallet', that buys are 'NEVER an endorsement', that he 'can sell at any time for any reason', and 'DON'T BLINDLY COPYTRADE ME'.
findings.evidence: Search-result snippets from his X posts (status 2093852462910177473, 2092581593802002618, 2091810338446455144 'i'm currently number one on...'), TronWeekly/Arkham article, BTCC deep article (PONS buy size), KuCoin KOL top-10 list, invezz profile, CoinGecko 'BONK GUY WAS RIGHT' token page. Leaderboard numbers from local fomoapi JSON.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Largest follower base on fomo; his buys move thin Robinhood Chain pools. Following him is late by construction (his cost basis is ~10x below current). His own disclaimer that he sells without notice, plus the 25%-adjusted-PnL critique, mark him as exit-liquidity risk for copiers, not a copy target. Potential use: as a sentiment/flow signal (his buys trigger follower inflows) rather than as a position to mirror.

findings.claim: DumbCrayonEater: #2 on 7d/30d/all fomo leaderboards ($6.5M/$8.7M/$9.35M; 451.3K fomo followers). Not a legacy KOL; became famous in late Aug/early Sept 2026 for spending ~$21.2K over two months accumulating 29.32M AI (Artificial Inu, LONG-launched, NVDA-paired token on Robinhood Chain), worth ~$8.1M on 2026-09-02 (~382x), making them the largest AI holder; per fomo data $AI is ~91% of the portfolio. Gains are entirely unrealized; coverage notes it is 'relatively unlikely that the eventual realized gains would match'. Has a TikTok presence posting Solana memecoin PnL content. Style: slow batch accumulation from ~$15M mcap, then hold. No evidence found of launching tokens, running clans, or dumping.
findings.evidence: Lookonchain-sourced coverage via BlockBeats and bitcoinethereumnews (citing 'FOMOFamily via Lookonchain'); search snippet '$AI represents 91% of their holdings' on FOMO; TikTok discover snippet. Local leaderboard: 2,240 trades, $1.01M volume, 79 holdings.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Archetype of 'one illiquid bag = leaderboard #2'. As largest holder of a ~$300M-cap token, the position cannot be exited near mark; the leaderboard PnL is not a realizable edge. Their pre-pump accumulation pattern (small buys over weeks in a LONG stock-paired token) is the interesting, possibly replicable behavior, not the current rank.

findings.claim: Salem1299534: #3 on 7d/30d/all fomo ($5.1M/$6.6M/$6.6M; 178.6K fomo followers) with only 11 holdings and 1,115 trades on $2.38M volume. Listed in KuCoin/Solana Daily's 'top 10 KOLs on Fomo by 7D PnL' but no X profile, media coverage, or identity was found (the handle format suggests an auto-generated X username). Peer.family tracked a recent -13.1% swing. No evidence found either way on token launching, clans, or dumping.
findings.evidence: KuCoin KOL top-10 list (@Salem1299534); peer.family listing; local leaderboard JSON. Web searches for the handle on X returned nothing.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Large PnL concentrated in very few holdings with an anonymous, non-KOL profile: could be a genuinely skilled concentrated trader or a wallet marking up one bag. Needs on-chain holdings breakdown (fomoapi trades/balances) before any conclusion.

findings.claim: Natan_benish (Nate): co-founder of LONG (long.xyz), the Robinhood Chain launchpad that pairs new tokens against tokenized stocks (NVDA, TSLA, HIMS, SPCX...) with ~13% platform fees per a KuCoin write-up; LONG launched AI (Artificial Inu), BONER, SPACEHOOD and passed $425M tokenized-stock volume. Earlier he built NIM Network / an AI meme-maker / Xenopus AI framework. He is #4 on fomo 7d/30d/all ($4.2M/$5.25M/$5.24M; 77.4K fomo followers) with only $12.6K cumulative fomo volume across 1,891 trades — his leaderboard PnL is therefore almost certainly appreciation on tokens acquired outside fomo (plausibly LONG-launched tokens), not fomo trading.
findings.evidence: KuCoin LONG article ('Nate (@Natan_benish)... co-founder'; ~13% fees); MEXC Learn on long.xyz (Nate; AI/BONER/SPACEHOOD; 'no plans for a separate platform token'); search snippets on LONG volume and NIM/XENO; local leaderboard JSON ratio.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Launchpad founder on the leaderboard is a structural insider (fee recipient, first-mover on his own launches). His rank is not a trading signal; but LONG-launched, stock-paired tokens (AI, BONER) produced the biggest Aug-Sept winners and are a distinct venue/meta worth modeling separately from Pons.

findings.claim: brrrgrrrz ('Burgz' on fomo; X @brrrgrrrz 'joe', bio 'It's immoral to let a sucker keep his money'): #5 on fomo 7d/30d/all ($3.57M/$4.51M/$4.61M; 73.1K fomo followers, 19 holdings, 2,415 trades on $4.0M volume, PnL/volume ~1.15x). Search results associate the same 'joe' persona with the SolBurgerz / 'Big Kahuna Burger' Solana memecoin account (posts about 'Nailong revolution', celebrity shilling), suggesting prior involvement running or promoting a memecoin — but this link is inferred from search snippets only. No media profile exists.
findings.evidence: X search result: 'joe (@brrrgrrrz)' bio; SolBurgerz posts surfaced under the same 'joe' name in results for the handle. Local leaderboard JSON for fomo stats.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Cynical self-description plus possible token-promoter history are consistent with a predator profile (sells into follower flow). Balanced PnL/volume suggests active realized trading rather than one bag — worth pulling trade history to test if his buys precede follower inflows and his sells follow them.
